## Allow underscores as first character in model name parts

We need to update the model name validation logic to permit underscores as the starting character for any part of a model name (host, namespace, model, tag, and digest). Currently, the validation requires the first character of each part to be alphanumeric (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). The goal is to allow names that begin with an underscore, such as `_why/_the/_lucky:_stiff`.

    Additionally, update the mac app's welcome screen to show the command `ollama run llama3` instead of the outdated `ollama run llama2`.

    Please ensure all tests pass and that the documentation comments in `types/model/name.go` accurately reflect the new validation rules.

## Environment Setup
Check the `go.mod` file for Go module configuration and dependencies. Review `types/model/name_test.go` for existing test patterns. The `Makefile` and `.github/workflows/test.yaml` may contain test running instructions. Also check `macapp/package.json` and `macapp/README.md` for frontend setup details.

## Implementation Plan
1. Modify the `isValidPart` function in `types/model/name.go` so that the first character check uses `isAlphanumericOrUnderscore` instead of `isAlphanumeric`.
    2. Add a new helper function `isAlphanumericOrUnderscore` that returns true for alphanumeric characters or underscore, and update the existing `isAlphanumeric` function to delegate to it or keep both as needed.
    3. Update all documentation comments in `types/model/name.go` that describe the character patterns for each name part to reflect that underscores are now allowed as the first character.
    4. Add a test case in `types/model/name_test.go` for a valid name starting with underscores (e.g., `_why/_the/_lucky:_stiff`), and remove any unused logging statements from the test file.
    5. Update `macapp/src/app.tsx` to change the `command` variable from `'ollama run llama2'` to `'ollama run llama3'`.

conversation.content:
We need to extend the Windows build pipeline to support ARM64 in addition to the existing amd64 target. Currently the build scripts and installer are hardcoded to use amd64-specific paths and architecture flags, preventing us from producing ARM64 Windows binaries. Additionally, there is a bug where the model scheduler on CPU-only systems (including ARM64, which has no GPU support) can unnecessarily unload loaded models to make room for new ones, even when the configuration allows multiple models to be loaded concurrently. We also need to block copying a model onto itself, which currently is allowed and causes issues.

    The goal is to make the Windows build process architecture-aware so that the same scripts work for both amd64 and arm64, and to fix the scheduler so CPU-only environments load new models without evicting existing ones. This is a minimal, focused change — don't refactor the build system or scheduler generally.

    Please ensure environment detection is based on the actual processor architecture rather than a hardcoded value, and that AVX/AVX2-specific runners are not built on ARM64 systems.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files in the repository for build and test setup:
    - `scripts/build_windows.ps1` — Windows build script (drive the build process)
    - `llm/generate/gen_windows.ps1` — architecture-specific LLM runner generation
    - `app/ollama.iss` — Inno Setup installer configuration
    - `llm/llm.go` — cgo LDFLAGS for different architectures
    - `go.mod` / `go.sum` — Go module dependencies
    - `server/sched_test.go` — scheduler tests
    - `.github/workflows/test.yaml` — CI test workflow

## Implementation Plan
1. Update `llm/generate/gen_windows.ps1`: derive `$script:ARCH` from `$Env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` (lowercase) instead of hardcoding "amd64". Skip building AVX/AVX2 variants and CUDA/ROCm runners when targeting ARM64; for ARM64, pass `-A ARM64` to cmake for CPU builds.
    2. Update `scripts/build_windows.ps1`: determine `TARGET_ARCH` from environment, use `dist/windows-${TARGET_ARCH}` directory paths, pass the architecture to the Inno Setup installer via a `/DARCH=` define, and name the distribution zip accordingly.
    3. Update `app/ollama.iss`: replace hardcoded `dist\windows-amd64` sources with `dist\windows-{#ARCH}` and use a conditional to include ROCm only for amd64.
    4. Add the `#cgo windows,arm64` LDFLAGS line in `llm/llm.go` so the Go binary can link the ARM64 static library.
    5. Update `server/sched.go`: when the system is in CPU-only mode (single CPU GPU library or `NumGPU == 0`), load the model immediately without checking GPU memory fitting or evicting existing runners; simply enforce the `loadedMax` limit. Add corresponding test coverage in `server/sched_test.go`.
    6. In `server/images.go`, add a guard in `CopyModel` to return early (no-op success) if the source and destination model file paths are identical, preventing self-copy.

54: 		m, err := strconv.Atoi(maxRunners)
55: 		if err != nil {
56: 			slog.Error("invalid setting", "OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS", maxRunners, "error", err)
57: 		} else {
58: 			loadedMax = m
59: 		}
60: 	}
61: 	if onp := os.Getenv("OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL"); onp != "" {
62: 		p, err := strconv.Atoi(onp)
63: 		if err != nil || p <= 0 {
64: 			slog.Error("invalid parallel setting, must be greater than zero", "OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL", onp, "error", err)
65: 		} else {
66: 			numParallel = p
67: 		}
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	sched := &Scheduler{
71: 		pendingReqCh:  make(chan *LlmRequest, maxQueuedRequests),
72: 		finishedReqCh: make(chan *LlmRequest, maxQueuedRequests),
73: 		expiredCh:     make(chan *runnerRef, maxQueuedRequests),
74: 		unloadedCh:    make(chan interface{}, maxQueuedRequests),
75: 		loaded:        make(map[string]*runnerRef),
76: 		newServerFn:   llm.NewLlamaServer,
77: 		getGpuFn:      gpu.GetGPUInfo,
78: 	}
79: 	sched.loadFn = sched.load
80: 	return sched
81: }

84: func (s *Scheduler) GetRunner(c context.Context, model *Model, opts api.Options, sessionDuration time.Duration) (chan *runnerRef, chan error) {
85: 	req := &LlmRequest{
86: 		ctx:             c,
87: 		model:           model,
88: 		opts:            opts,
89: 		sessionDuration: sessionDuration,
90: 		successCh:       make(chan *runnerRef),
91: 		errCh:           make(chan error, 1),
92: 	}
93: 	// context split across parallel threads
94: 	opts.NumCtx = opts.NumCtx * numParallel
95: 	select {
96: 	case s.pendingReqCh <- req:
97: 	default:
98: 		req.errCh <- fmt.Errorf("server busy, please try again.  maximum pending requests exceeded")
99: 	}
100: 	return req.successCh, req.errCh
101: }

103: // Returns immediately, spawns go routines for the scheduler which will shutdown when ctx is done
104: func (s *Scheduler) Run(ctx context.Context) {
105: 	slog.Debug("starting llm scheduler")
106: 	go func() {
107: 		s.processPending(ctx)
108: 	}()
109: 
110: 	go func() {
111: 		s.processCompleted(ctx)
112: 	}()
113: }

115: func (s *Scheduler) processPending(ctx context.Context) {
116: 	for {
117: 		select {
118: 		case <-ctx.Done():
119: 			slog.Debug("shutting down scheduler pending loop")
120: 			return
121: 		case pending := <-s.pendingReqCh:
122: 			// Block other requests until we get this pending request running
123: 			for {
124: 				var runnerToExpire *runnerRef
125: 				s.loadedMu.Lock()
126: 				runner := s.loaded[pending.model.ModelPath]
127: 				loadedCount := len(s.loaded)
128: 				s.loadedMu.Unlock()
129: 				if runner != nil {
130: 					if runner.needsReload(ctx, pending) {
131: 						runnerToExpire = runner
132: 					} else {
133: 						// Runner is usable, return it
134: 						pending.useLoadedRunner(runner, s.finishedReqCh)
135: 						break
136: 					}
137: 				} else if loadedMax > 0 && loadedCount >= loadedMax {
138: 					slog.Debug("max runners achieved, unloading one to make room", "runner_count", loadedCount)
139: 					runnerToExpire = s.findRunnerToUnload(pending)
140: 				} else {
141: 					// Either no models are loaded or below loadedMax
142: 					// Get a refreshed GPU list
143: 					gpus := s.getGpuFn()
144: 
145: 					// Load model for fitting
146: 					ggml, err := llm.LoadModel(pending.model.ModelPath)
147: 					if err != nil {
148: 						pending.errCh <- err
149: 						break
150: 					}
151: 
152: 					// No models loaded. Load the model but prefer the best fit.
153: 					if loadedCount == 0 {
154: 						slog.Debug("loading first model", "model", pending.model.ModelPath)
155: 						g := pickBestFitGPUs(pending, ggml, gpus)
156: 						if g != nil {
157: 							gpus = g
158: 						}
159: 						s.loadFn(pending, ggml, gpus)
160: 						break
161: 					}
162: 
163: 					// More than one loaded model, so we have to see if the new one fits
164: 					// Update free memory from currently loaded models
165: 					s.updateFreeSpace(gpus)
166: 					gpus = pickBestFitGPUs(pending, ggml, gpus)
167: 					if gpus != nil {
168: 						slog.Debug("new model fits with existing models, loading")
169: 						s.loadFn(pending, ggml, gpus)
170: 						break
171: 					}
172: 					runnerToExpire = s.findRunnerToUnload(pending)
173: 				}
174: 
175: 				if runnerToExpire == nil {
176: 					// Shouildn't happen
177: 					slog.Error("runner to expire was nil!")
178: 					continue
179: 				}
180: 				// Trigger an expiration to unload once it's done
181: 				runnerToExpire.refMu.Lock()
182: 				slog.Debug("resetting model to expire immediately to make room", "model", runnerToExpire.model, "refCount", runnerToExpire.refCount)
183: 				if runnerToExpire.expireTimer != nil {
184: 					runnerToExpire.expireTimer.Stop()
185: 					runnerToExpire.expireTimer = nil
186: 				}
187: 				runnerToExpire.sessionDuration = 0
188: 				if runnerToExpire.refCount <= 0 {
189: 					s.expiredCh <- runnerToExpire
190: 				}
191: 				runnerToExpire.refMu.Unlock()
192: 				// Wait for the unload to happen
193: 				// Note: at this point we're queueing up all incoming requests, even if they were for
194: 				// a different model that's loaded and not scheduled to be removed.
195: 				slog.Debug("waiting for pending requests to complete and unload to occur", "model", runnerToExpire.model)
196: 				select {
197: 				case <-ctx.Done():
198: 					slog.Debug("shutting down scheduler pending loop")
199: 					return
200: 				case <-s.unloadedCh:
201: 					slog.Debug("unload completed", "model", runnerToExpire.model)
202: 					continue
203: 				}
204: 			}
205: 		case <-s.unloadedCh:
206: 			// An unload request when there are no pending request can be ignored
207: 			slog.Debug("ignoring unload event with no pending requests")
208: 		}
209: 	}
210: }

212: func (s *Scheduler) processCompleted(ctx context.Context) {
213: 	// Process completed requests, expired timers, and unloading models
214: 	for {
215: 		select {
216: 		case <-ctx.Done():
217: 			slog.Debug("shutting down scheduler completed loop")
218: 			return
219: 		case finished := <-s.finishedReqCh:
220: 			s.loadedMu.Lock()
221: 			runner := s.loaded[finished.model.ModelPath]
222: 			s.loadedMu.Unlock()
223: 			if runner == nil {
224: 				slog.Error("finished requeset signal received after model unloaded", "model", finished.model.ModelPath)
225: 				continue
226: 			}
227: 			runner.refMu.Lock()
228: 			runner.refCount--
229: 			if runner.refCount <= 0 {
230: 				if runner.sessionDuration <= 0 {
231: 					slog.Debug("runner with zero duration has gone idle, expiring to unload", "model", runner.model)
232: 					if runner.expireTimer != nil {
233: 						runner.expireTimer.Stop()
234: 						runner.expireTimer = nil
235: 					}
236: 					s.expiredCh <- runner
237: 				} else if runner.expireTimer == nil {
238: 					slog.Debug("runner with non-zero duration has gone idle, adding timer", "model", runner.model, "duration", runner.sessionDuration)
239: 					runner.expireTimer = time.AfterFunc(runner.sessionDuration, func() {
240: 						slog.Debug("timer expired, expiring to unload", "model", runner.model)
241: 						runner.refMu.Lock()
242: 						defer runner.refMu.Unlock()
243: 						if runner.expireTimer != nil {
244: 							runner.expireTimer.Stop()
245: 						}
246: 						s.expiredCh <- runner
247: 					})
248: 				} else {
249: 					slog.Debug("runner with non-zero duration has gone idle, resetting timer", "model", runner.model, "duration", runner.sessionDuration)
250: 					runner.expireTimer.Reset(runner.sessionDuration)
251: 				}
252: 			}
253: 			slog.Debug("after processing request finished event", "model", runner.model, "refCount", runner.refCount)
254: 			runner.refMu.Unlock()
255: 		case runner := <-s.expiredCh:
256: 			slog.Debug("runner expired event received", "model", runner.model)
257: 			runner.refMu.Lock()
258: 			if runner.refCount > 0 {
259: 				// Shouldn't happen, but safeguard to ensure no leaked runners
260: 				slog.Debug("expired event with positive ref count, retrying", "model", runner.model, "refCount", runner.refCount)
261: 				go func(runner *runnerRef) {
262: 					// We can't unload yet, but want to as soon as the current request completes
263: 					// So queue up another expired event
264: 					time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
265: 					s.expiredCh <- runner
266: 				}(runner)
267: 				runner.refMu.Unlock()
268: 				continue
269: 			}
270: 
271: 			slog.Debug("got lock to unload", "model", runner.model)
272: 			runner.unload()
273: 			s.loadedMu.Lock()
274: 			delete(s.loaded, runner.model)
275: 			s.loadedMu.Unlock()
276: 			slog.Debug("runner released", "model", runner.model)
277: 			runner.refMu.Unlock()
278: 			slog.Debug("sending an unloaded event", "model", runner.model)
279: 			s.unloadedCh <- struct{}{}
280: 		}
281: 	}
282: }

286: // Updates session duration, and resets expiration timer
287: func (pending *LlmRequest) useLoadedRunner(runner *runnerRef, finished chan *LlmRequest) {
288: 	runner.refMu.Lock()
289: 	defer runner.refMu.Unlock()
290: 	runner.refCount++
291: 	runner.sessionDuration = pending.sessionDuration
292: 	pending.successCh <- runner
293: 	go func() {
294: 		<-pending.ctx.Done()
295: 		slog.Debug("context for request finished")
296: 		finished <- pending
297: 	}()

300: func (s *Scheduler) load(req *LlmRequest, ggml *llm.GGML, gpus gpu.GpuInfoList) {
301: 	llama, err := s.newServerFn(gpus, req.model.ModelPath, ggml, req.model.AdapterPaths, req.model.ProjectorPaths, req.opts)
302: 	if err != nil {
303: 		// some older models are not compatible with newer versions of llama.cpp
304: 		// show a generalized compatibility error until there is a better way to
305: 		// check for model compatibility
306: 		if errors.Is(llm.ErrUnsupportedFormat, err) || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "failed to load model") {
307: 			err = fmt.Errorf("%v: this model may be incompatible with your version of Ollama. If you previously pulled this model, try updating it by running `ollama pull %s`", err, req.model.ShortName)
308: 		}
309: 		slog.Info("NewLlamaServer failed", "model", req.model.ModelPath, "error", err)
310: 		req.errCh <- err
311: 		return
312: 	}
313: 	runner := &runnerRef{}
314: 	runner.model = req.model.ModelPath
315: 	runner.adapters = req.model.AdapterPaths
316: 	runner.projectors = req.model.ProjectorPaths
317: 	runner.llama = llama
318: 	runner.Options = &req.opts
319: 	runner.sessionDuration = req.sessionDuration
320: 	runner.gpus = gpus
321: 	runner.estimatedVRAM = llama.EstimatedVRAM()
322: 	runner.loading = true
323: 	runner.refCount = 1
324: 	runner.refMu.Lock()
325: 	s.loadedMu.Lock()
326: 	s.loaded[req.model.ModelPath] = runner
327: 	slog.Info("loaded runners", "count", len(s.loaded))
328: 	s.loadedMu.Unlock()
329: 
330: 	go func() {
331: 		defer runner.refMu.Unlock()
332: 		if err = llama.WaitUntilRunning(req.ctx); err != nil {
333: 			slog.Error("error loading llama server", "error", err)
334: 			runner.refCount--
335: 			req.errCh <- err
336: 			slog.Debug("triggering expiration for failed load", "model", runner.model)
337: 			s.expiredCh <- runner
338: 			return
339: 		}
340: 		slog.Debug("finished setting up runner", "model", req.model.ModelPath)
341: 		runner.loading = false
342: 		go func() {
343: 			<-req.ctx.Done()
344: 			slog.Debug("context for request finished")
345: 			s.finishedReqCh <- req
346: 		}()
347: 		req.successCh <- runner
348: 	}()
349: }

351: func (s *Scheduler) updateFreeSpace(allGpus gpu.GpuInfoList) {
352: 	type predKey struct {
353: 		Library string
354: 		ID      string
355: 	}
356: 	predMap := map[predKey]uint64{} // Sum up the total predicted usage per GPU for all runners
357: 	s.loadedMu.Lock()
358: 	for _, r := range s.loaded {
359: 		r.refMu.Lock()
360: 		gpuIDs := make([]string, 0, len(r.gpus))
361: 		if r.llama != nil {
362: 
363: 			// TODO this should be broken down by GPU instead of assuming uniform spread
364: 			estimatedVRAMPerGPU := r.llama.EstimatedVRAM() / uint64(len(r.gpus))
365: 			for _, gpu := range r.gpus {
366: 				gpuIDs = append(gpuIDs, gpu.ID)
367: 			}
368: 			for _, gpu := range allGpus {
369: 				if slices.Contains(gpuIDs, gpu.ID) {
370: 					predMap[predKey{gpu.Library, gpu.ID}] += estimatedVRAMPerGPU
371: 				}
372: 			}
373: 		} else {
374: 			slog.Warn("unexpected nil runner reference, memory prediction may be incorrect")
375: 		}
376: 		r.refMu.Unlock()
377: 	}
378: 	s.loadedMu.Unlock()
379: 
380: 	// Now that we've summed up all the GPU usage predictions across all the loaded runners, update the gpu list
381: 	for i := range allGpus {
382: 		if p, ok := predMap[predKey{allGpus[i].Library, allGpus[i].ID}]; ok {
383: 			slog.Debug("gpu reported", "gpu", allGpus[i].ID, "library", allGpus[i].Library, "available", format.HumanBytes2(allGpus[i].FreeMemory))
384: 			if p > allGpus[i].TotalMemory {
385: 				// Shouldn't happen
386: 				slog.Warn("predicted usage exceeds VRAM", "gpu", allGpus[i].ID, "totalMemory", allGpus[i].TotalMemory, "predicted", p)
387: 				allGpus[i].FreeMemory = 0
388: 			} else if (allGpus[i].TotalMemory - p) < allGpus[i].FreeMemory { // predicted free is smaller than reported free, use it
389: 				// TODO maybe we should just always trust our numbers, since cuda's free memory reporting is laggy
390: 				// and we might unload models we didn't actually need to.  The risk is if some other GPU intensive app is loaded
391: 				// after we start our first runner, then we'll never acount for that, so picking the smallest free value seems prudent.
392: 				allGpus[i].FreeMemory = allGpus[i].TotalMemory - p
393: 			}
394: 			slog.Info("updated VRAM", "gpu", allGpus[i].ID, "library", allGpus[i].Library, "total", format.HumanBytes2(allGpus[i].TotalMemory), "available", format.HumanBytes2(allGpus[i].FreeMemory))
395: 		}
396: 	}
397: }

431: func (runner *runnerRef) needsReload(ctx context.Context, req *LlmRequest) bool {
432: 	slog.Debug("evaluating already loaded", "model", req.model.ModelPath)
433: 	runner.refMu.Lock()
434: 	defer runner.refMu.Unlock()
435: 
436: 	timeout := 10 * time.Second
437: 	if runner.loading {
438: 		timeout = 2 * time.Minute // Initial load can take a long time for big models on slow systems...
439: 	}
440: 
441: 	// Don't reload runner if num_gpu=-1 was provided
442: 	optsExisting := runner.Options.Runner
443: 	optsNew := req.opts.Runner
444: 	if optsNew.NumGPU < 0 {
445: 		optsExisting.NumGPU = -1
446: 		optsNew.NumGPU = -1
447: 	}
448: 
449: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
450: 	defer cancel()
451: 	if !reflect.DeepEqual(runner.adapters, req.model.AdapterPaths) || // have the adapters changed?
452: 		!reflect.DeepEqual(runner.projectors, req.model.ProjectorPaths) || // have the projectors changed?
453: 		!reflect.DeepEqual(optsExisting, optsNew) || // have the runner options changed?
454: 		runner.llama.Ping(ctx) != nil {
455: 		return true
456: 	}
457: 
458: 	return false
459: }

463: func (a ByDuration) Len() int      { return len(a) }
464: func (a ByDuration) Swap(i, j int) { a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i] }
465: func (a ByDuration) Less(i, j int) bool {
466: 	// uint64 to turn negative time (never unload) to largest
467: 	return uint64(a[i].sessionDuration) < uint64(a[j].sessionDuration)

476: // pickBestFitGPUs will try to find the optimal placement of the model in the available GPUs where the model fully fits
477: // If the model can not be fit fully within the available GPU(s) nil is returned
478: func pickBestFitGPUs(req *LlmRequest, ggml *llm.GGML, gpus gpu.GpuInfoList) gpu.GpuInfoList {
479: 	var estimatedVRAM uint64
480: 	for _, gl := range gpus.ByLibrary() {
481: 		var ok bool
482: 		sgl := append(make(gpu.GpuInfoList, 0, len(gl)), gl...)
483: 
484: 		// TODO - potentially sort by performance capability, existing models loaded, etc.
485: 		// Note: at present, this will favor more VRAM over faster GPU speed in mixed setups
486: 		sort.Sort(sort.Reverse(gpu.ByFreeMemory(sgl)))
487: 
488: 		// First attempt to fit the model into a single GPU
489: 		for _, g := range sgl {
490: 			if ok, estimatedVRAM = llm.PredictServerFit([]gpu.GpuInfo{g}, ggml, req.model.AdapterPaths, req.model.ProjectorPaths, req.opts); ok {
491: 				slog.Debug("new model will fit in available VRAM in single GPU, loading", "model", req.model.ModelPath, "gpu", g.ID, "available", g.FreeMemory, "required", format.HumanBytes2(estimatedVRAM))
492: 				return []gpu.GpuInfo{g}
493: 			}
494: 		}
495: 
496: 		// TODO future refinements
497: 		// - if multiple Libraries, see if any single GPU in any Library will fit
498: 		// - try subsets of GPUs instead of just falling back to 1 or all in a family
499: 
500: 		// Now try all the GPUs
501: 		if ok, estimatedVRAM = llm.PredictServerFit(gl, ggml, req.model.AdapterPaths, req.model.ProjectorPaths, req.opts); ok {
502: 			slog.Debug("new model will fit in available VRAM, loading", "model", req.model.ModelPath, "library", gl[0].Library, "required", format.HumanBytes2(estimatedVRAM))
503: 			return gl
504: 		}
505: 	}
506: 	return nil
507: }

509: // findRunnerToUnload finds a runner to unload to make room for a new model
510: func (s *Scheduler) findRunnerToUnload(req *LlmRequest) *runnerRef {
511: 	s.loadedMu.Lock()
512: 	runnerList := make([]*runnerRef, 0, len(s.loaded))
513: 	for _, r := range s.loaded {
514: 		runnerList = append(runnerList, r)
515: 	}
516: 	s.loadedMu.Unlock()
517: 
518: 	// In the future we can enhance the algorithm to be smarter about picking the optimal runner to unload
519: 	// e.g., if we have multiple options, will one make room for the request?
520: 	sort.Sort(ByDuration(runnerList))
521: 
522: 	// First try to find a runner that's already idle
523: 	for _, runner := range runnerList {
524: 		runner.refMu.Lock()
525: 		rc := runner.refCount
526: 		runner.refMu.Unlock()
527: 		if rc == 0 {
528: 			slog.Debug("found an idle runner to unload")
529: 			return runner
530: 		}
531: 	}
532: 	// None appear idle, just wait for the one with the shortest duration
533: 	slog.Debug("no idle runners, picking the shortest duration", "count", len(runnerList))
534: 	return runnerList[0]
535: }

133: func GetManifest(mp ModelPath) (*ManifestV2, string, error) {
134: 	fp, err := mp.GetManifestPath()
135: 	if err != nil {
136: 		return nil, "", err
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	if _, err = os.Stat(fp); err != nil {
140: 		return nil, "", err
141: 	}
142: 
143: 	var manifest *ManifestV2
144: 
145: 	bts, err := os.ReadFile(fp)
146: 	if err != nil {
147: 		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("couldn't open file '%s'", fp)
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	shaSum := sha256.Sum256(bts)
151: 	shaStr := hex.EncodeToString(shaSum[:])
152: 
153: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(bts, &manifest); err != nil {
154: 		return nil, "", err
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	return manifest, shaStr, nil
158: }

160: func GetModel(name string) (*Model, error) {
161: 	mp := ParseModelPath(name)
162: 	manifest, digest, err := GetManifest(mp)
163: 	if err != nil {
164: 		return nil, err
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	model := &Model{
168: 		Name:      mp.GetFullTagname(),
169: 		ShortName: mp.GetShortTagname(),
170: 		Digest:    digest,
171: 		Template:  "{{ .Prompt }}",
172: 		License:   []string{},
173: 		Size:      manifest.GetTotalSize(),
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	filename, err := GetBlobsPath(manifest.Config.Digest)
177: 	if err != nil {
178: 		return nil, err
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	configFile, err := os.Open(filename)
182: 	if err != nil {
183: 		return nil, err
184: 	}
185: 	defer configFile.Close()
186: 
187: 	if err := json.NewDecoder(configFile).Decode(&model.Config); err != nil {
188: 		return nil, err
189: 	}
190: 
191: 	for _, layer := range manifest.Layers {
192: 		filename, err := GetBlobsPath(layer.Digest)
193: 		if err != nil {
194: 			return nil, err
195: 		}
196: 
197: 		switch layer.MediaType {
198: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.model":
199: 			model.ModelPath = filename
200: 			model.ParentModel = layer.From
201: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.embed":
202: 			// Deprecated in versions  > 0.1.2
203: 			// TODO: remove this warning in a future version
204: 			slog.Info("WARNING: model contains embeddings, but embeddings in modelfiles have been deprecated and will be ignored.")
205: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.adapter":
206: 			model.AdapterPaths = append(model.AdapterPaths, filename)
207: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.projector":
208: 			model.ProjectorPaths = append(model.ProjectorPaths, filename)
209: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.template":
210: 			bts, err := os.ReadFile(filename)
211: 			if err != nil {
212: 				return nil, err
213: 			}
214: 
215: 			model.Template = string(bts)
216: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.system":
217: 			bts, err := os.ReadFile(filename)
218: 			if err != nil {
219: 				return nil, err
220: 			}
221: 
222: 			model.System = string(bts)
223: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.prompt":
224: 			bts, err := os.ReadFile(filename)
225: 			if err != nil {
226: 				return nil, err
227: 			}
228: 
229: 			model.Template = string(bts)
230: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.params":
231: 			params, err := os.Open(filename)
232: 			if err != nil {
233: 				return nil, err
234: 			}
235: 			defer params.Close()
236: 
237: 			// parse model options parameters into a map so that we can see which fields have been specified explicitly
238: 			if err = json.NewDecoder(params).Decode(&model.Options); err != nil {
239: 				return nil, err
240: 			}
241: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.messages":
242: 			msgs, err := os.Open(filename)
243: 			if err != nil {
244: 				return nil, err
245: 			}
246: 			defer msgs.Close()
247: 
248: 			if err = json.NewDecoder(msgs).Decode(&model.Messages); err != nil {
249: 				return nil, err
250: 			}
251: 		case "application/vnd.ollama.image.license":
252: 			bts, err := os.ReadFile(filename)
253: 			if err != nil {
254: 				return nil, err
255: 			}
256: 			model.License = append(model.License, string(bts))
257: 		}
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	return model, nil
261: }

263: func realpath(mfDir, from string) string {
264: 	abspath, err := filepath.Abs(from)
265: 	if err != nil {
266: 		return from
267: 	}
268: 
269: 	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
270: 	if err != nil {
271: 		return abspath
272: 	}
273: 
274: 	if from == "~" {
275: 		return home
276: 	} else if strings.HasPrefix(from, "~/") {
277: 		return filepath.Join(home, from[2:])
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(mfDir, from)); err == nil {
281: 		// this is a file relative to the Modelfile
282: 		return filepath.Join(mfDir, from)
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	return abspath
286: }

288: func CreateModel(ctx context.Context, name, modelFileDir, quantization string, commands []parser.Command, fn func(resp api.ProgressResponse)) error {
289: 	deleteMap := make(map[string]struct{})
290: 	if manifest, _, err := GetManifest(ParseModelPath(name)); err == nil {
291: 		for _, layer := range append(manifest.Layers, manifest.Config) {
292: 			deleteMap[layer.Digest] = struct{}{}
293: 		}
294: 	}
295: 
296: 	config := ConfigV2{
297: 		OS:           "linux",
298: 		Architecture: "amd64",
299: 		RootFS: RootFS{
300: 			Type: "layers",
301: 		},
302: 	}
303: 
304: 	var layers Layers
305: 	messages := []string{}
306: 
307: 	params := make(map[string][]string)
308: 	fromParams := make(map[string]any)
309: 
310: 	for _, c := range commands {
311: 		mediatype := fmt.Sprintf("application/vnd.ollama.image.%s", c.Name)
312: 
313: 		switch c.Name {
314: 		case "model":
315: 			if strings.HasPrefix(c.Args, "@") {
316: 				blobPath, err := GetBlobsPath(strings.TrimPrefix(c.Args, "@"))
317: 				if err != nil {
318: 					return err
319: 				}
320: 
321: 				c.Args = blobPath
322: 			}
323: 
324: 			pathName := realpath(modelFileDir, c.Args)
325: 
326: 			ggufName, err := convertModel(name, pathName, fn)
327: 			if err != nil {
328: 				var pathErr *fs.PathError
329: 				switch {
330: 				case errors.Is(err, zip.ErrFormat):
331: 					// it's not a safetensor archive
332: 				case errors.As(err, &pathErr):
333: 					// it's not a file on disk, could be a model reference
334: 				default:
335: 					return err
336: 				}
337: 			}
338: 
339: 			if ggufName != "" {
340: 				pathName = ggufName
341: 				defer os.RemoveAll(ggufName)
342: 
343: 				if quantization != "" {
344: 					quantization = strings.ToUpper(quantization)
345: 					fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: fmt.Sprintf("quantizing %s model to %s", "F16", quantization)})
346: 					tempfile, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(ggufName), quantization)
347: 					if err != nil {
348: 						return err
349: 					}
350: 					defer os.RemoveAll(tempfile.Name())
351: 
352: 					if err := llm.Quantize(ggufName, tempfile.Name(), quantization); err != nil {
353: 						return err
354: 					}
355: 
356: 					if err := tempfile.Close(); err != nil {
357: 						return err
358: 					}
359: 
360: 					pathName = tempfile.Name()
361: 				}
362: 			}
363: 
364: 			bin, err := os.Open(pathName)
365: 			if err != nil {
366: 				// not a file on disk so must be a model reference
367: 				modelpath := ParseModelPath(c.Args)
368: 				manifest, _, err := GetManifest(modelpath)
369: 				switch {
370: 				case errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
371: 					fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "pulling model"})
372: 					if err := PullModel(ctx, c.Args, &registryOptions{}, fn); err != nil {
373: 						return err
374: 					}
375: 
376: 					manifest, _, err = GetManifest(modelpath)
377: 					if err != nil {
378: 						return err
379: 					}
380: 				case err != nil:
381: 					return err
382: 				}
383: 
384: 				fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "reading model metadata"})
385: 				fromConfigPath, err := GetBlobsPath(manifest.Config.Digest)
386: 				if err != nil {
387: 					return err
388: 				}
389: 
390: 				fromConfigFile, err := os.Open(fromConfigPath)
391: 				if err != nil {
392: 					return err
393: 				}
394: 				defer fromConfigFile.Close()
395: 
396: 				var fromConfig ConfigV2
397: 				if err := json.NewDecoder(fromConfigFile).Decode(&fromConfig); err != nil {
398: 					return err
399: 				}
400: 
401: 				// if the model is still not in gguf format, error out
402: 				if fromConfig.ModelFormat != "gguf" {
403: 					return fmt.Errorf("%s is not in gguf format, this base model is not compatible with this version of ollama", c.Args)
404: 				}
405: 
406: 				config.SetModelFormat(fromConfig.ModelFormat)
407: 				config.SetModelFamily(append(fromConfig.ModelFamilies, fromConfig.ModelFamily)...)
408: 				config.SetModelType(fromConfig.ModelType)
409: 				config.SetFileType(fromConfig.FileType)
410: 
411: 				for _, layer := range manifest.Layers {
412: 					deleteMap[layer.Digest] = struct{}{}
413: 					if layer.MediaType == "application/vnd.ollama.image.params" {
414: 						fromParamsPath, err := GetBlobsPath(layer.Digest)
415: 						if err != nil {
416: 							return err
417: 						}
418: 
419: 						fromParamsFile, err := os.Open(fromParamsPath)
420: 						if err != nil {
421: 							return err
422: 						}
423: 						defer fromParamsFile.Close()
424: 
425: 						if err := json.NewDecoder(fromParamsFile).Decode(&fromParams); err != nil {
426: 							return err
427: 						}
428: 					}
429: 
430: 					layer, err := NewLayerFromLayer(layer.Digest, layer.MediaType, modelpath.GetShortTagname())
431: 					if err != nil {
432: 						return err
433: 					}
434: 
435: 					layers.Add(layer)
436: 				}
437: 
438: 				deleteMap[manifest.Config.Digest] = struct{}{}
439: 				continue
440: 			}
441: 			defer bin.Close()
442: 
443: 			var offset int64
444: 			for {
445: 				fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "creating model layer"})
446: 				if _, err := bin.Seek(offset, io.SeekStart); err != nil {
447: 					return err
448: 				}
449: 
450: 				ggml, size, err := llm.DecodeGGML(bin)
451: 				if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
452: 					break
453: 				} else if errors.Is(err, llm.ErrUnsupportedFormat) {
454: 					return fmt.Errorf("model binary specified in FROM field is not a valid gguf format model, %w", err)
455: 				} else if err != nil {
456: 					return err
457: 				}
458: 
459: 				config.SetModelFormat(ggml.Name())
460: 				config.SetModelFamily(ggml.KV().Architecture())
461: 				config.SetModelType(format.HumanNumber(ggml.KV().ParameterCount()))
462: 				config.SetFileType(ggml.KV().FileType())
463: 
464: 				mediatype := mediatype
465: 				if ggml.KV().Architecture() == "clip" {
466: 					mediatype = "application/vnd.ollama.image.projector"
467: 				}
468: 
469: 				sr := io.NewSectionReader(bin, offset, size)
470: 				layer, err := NewLayer(sr, mediatype)
471: 				if err != nil {
472: 					return err
473: 				}
474: 
475: 				layers.Add(layer)
476: 
477: 				offset += size
478: 			}
479: 		case "adapter":
480: 			if strings.HasPrefix(c.Args, "@") {
481: 				blobPath, err := GetBlobsPath(strings.TrimPrefix(c.Args, "@"))
482: 				if err != nil {
483: 					return err
484: 				}
485: 
486: 				c.Args = blobPath
487: 			}
488: 
489: 			fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "creating adapter layer"})
490: 			bin, err := os.Open(realpath(modelFileDir, c.Args))
491: 			if err != nil {
492: 				return err
493: 			}
494: 			defer bin.Close()
495: 
496: 			_, size, err := llm.DecodeGGML(bin)
497: 			if err != nil {
498: 				return err
499: 			}
500: 
501: 			sr := io.NewSectionReader(bin, 0, size)
502: 			layer, err := NewLayer(sr, mediatype)
503: 			if err != nil {
504: 				return err
505: 			}
506: 
507: 			layers.Add(layer)
508: 		case "license":
509: 			fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "creating license layer"})
510: 
511: 			bin := strings.NewReader(c.Args)
512: 			layer, err := NewLayer(bin, mediatype)
513: 			if err != nil {
514: 				return err
515: 			}
516: 
517: 			layers.Add(layer)
518: 		case "template", "system":
519: 			fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: fmt.Sprintf("creating %s layer", c.Name)})
520: 
521: 			bin := strings.NewReader(c.Args)
522: 			layer, err := NewLayer(bin, mediatype)
523: 			if err != nil {
524: 				return err
525: 			}
526: 
527: 			layers.Replace(layer)
528: 		case "message":
529: 			messages = append(messages, c.Args)
530: 		default:
531: 			params[c.Name] = append(params[c.Name], c.Args)
532: 		}
533: 	}
534: 
535: 	if len(messages) > 0 {
536: 		fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "creating parameters layer"})
537: 
538: 		msgs := make([]api.Message, 0)
539: 
540: 		for _, m := range messages {
541: 			// todo: handle images
542: 			msg := strings.SplitN(m, ": ", 2)
543: 			msgs = append(msgs, api.Message{Role: msg[0], Content: msg[1]})
544: 		}
545: 
546: 		var b bytes.Buffer
547: 		if err := json.NewEncoder(&b).Encode(msgs); err != nil {
548: 			return err
549: 		}
550: 
551: 		layer, err := NewLayer(&b, "application/vnd.ollama.image.messages")
552: 		if err != nil {
553: 			return err
554: 		}
555: 
556: 		layers.Replace(layer)
557: 	}
558: 
559: 	if len(params) > 0 {
560: 		fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "creating parameters layer"})
561: 
562: 		formattedParams, err := api.FormatParams(params)
563: 		if err != nil {
564: 			return err
565: 		}
566: 
567: 		for k, v := range fromParams {
568: 			if _, ok := formattedParams[k]; !ok {
569: 				formattedParams[k] = v
570: 			}
571: 		}
572: 
573: 		var b bytes.Buffer
574: 		if err := json.NewEncoder(&b).Encode(formattedParams); err != nil {
575: 			return err
576: 		}
577: 
578: 		fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "creating config layer"})
579: 		layer, err := NewLayer(&b, "application/vnd.ollama.image.params")
580: 		if err != nil {
581: 			return err
582: 		}
583: 
584: 		layers.Replace(layer)
585: 	}
586: 
587: 	digests := make([]string, len(layers.items))
588: 	for i, layer := range layers.items {
589: 		digests[i] = layer.Digest
590: 	}
591: 
592: 	config.RootFS.DiffIDs = digests
593: 
594: 	var b bytes.Buffer
595: 	if err := json.NewEncoder(&b).Encode(config); err != nil {
596: 		return err
597: 	}
598: 
599: 	configLayer, err := NewLayer(&b, "application/vnd.docker.container.image.v1+json")
600: 	if err != nil {
601: 		return err
602: 	}
603: 
604: 	delete(deleteMap, configLayer.Digest)
605: 
606: 	for _, layer := range append(layers.items, configLayer) {
607: 		committed, err := layer.Commit()
608: 		if err != nil {
609: 			return err
610: 		}
611: 
612: 		status := "writing layer"
613: 		if !committed {
614: 			status = "using already created layer"
615: 		}
616: 
617: 		fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", status, layer.Digest)})
618: 
619: 		delete(deleteMap, layer.Digest)
620: 	}
621: 
622: 	fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "writing manifest"})
623: 	if err := WriteManifest(name, configLayer, layers.items); err != nil {
624: 		return err
625: 	}
626: 
627: 	if noprune := os.Getenv("OLLAMA_NOPRUNE"); noprune == "" {
628: 		if err := deleteUnusedLayers(nil, deleteMap, false); err != nil {
629: 			return err
630: 		}
631: 	}
632: 
633: 	fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "success"})
634: 	return nil
635: }

637: func convertModel(name, path string, fn func(resp api.ProgressResponse)) (string, error) {
638: 	r, err := zip.OpenReader(path)
639: 	if err != nil {
640: 		return "", err
641: 	}
642: 	defer r.Close()
643: 
644: 	tempDir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "ollama-convert")
645: 	if err != nil {
646: 		return "", err
647: 	}
648: 	defer os.RemoveAll(tempDir)
649: 
650: 	fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "unpacking model metadata"})
651: 	for _, f := range r.File {
652: 		fpath := filepath.Join(tempDir, f.Name)
653: 		outFile, err := os.OpenFile(fpath, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, f.Mode())
654: 		if err != nil {
655: 			return "", err
656: 		}
657: 
658: 		rc, err := f.Open()
659: 		if err != nil {
660: 			return "", err
661: 		}
662: 
663: 		_, err = io.Copy(outFile, rc)
664: 		if err != nil {
665: 			return "", err
666: 		}
667: 
668: 		outFile.Close()
669: 		rc.Close()
670: 	}
671: 
672: 	mf, err := convert.GetModelFormat(tempDir)
673: 	if err != nil {
674: 		return "", err
675: 	}
676: 
677: 	params, err := mf.GetParams(tempDir)
678: 	if err != nil {
679: 		return "", err
680: 	}
681: 
682: 	mArch, err := mf.GetModelArch(name, tempDir, params)
683: 	if err != nil {
684: 		return "", err
685: 	}
686: 
687: 	fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "processing tensors"})
688: 	if err := mArch.GetTensors(); err != nil {
689: 		return "", err
690: 	}
691: 
692: 	if err := mArch.LoadVocab(); err != nil {
693: 		return "", err
694: 	}
695: 
696: 	fn(api.ProgressResponse{Status: "converting model"})
697: 	path, err = mArch.WriteGGUF()
698: 	if err != nil {
699: 		return "", err

143: 	s, n.RawDigest, promised = cutLast(s, "@")

153: 	}
154: 	s, n.Namespace, promised = cutPromised(s, "/")

164: 		params = append(params, "--main-gpu", fmt.Sprintf("%d", opts.MainGPU))
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	if len(adapters) > 0 {
168: 		// TODO: applying multiple adapters is not supported by the llama.cpp server yet
169: 		params = append(params, "--lora", adapters[0])
170: 	}
171: 
172: 	if len(projectors) > 0 {
173: 		// TODO: applying multiple projectors is not supported by the llama.cpp server yet
174: 		params = append(params, "--mmproj", projectors[0])
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	if opts.NumThread > 0 {
178: 		params = append(params, "--threads", fmt.Sprintf("%d", opts.NumThread))
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	if !opts.F16KV {
182: 		params = append(params, "--memory-f32")
183: 	}
184: 
185: 	if opts.UseMLock {
186: 		params = append(params, "--mlock")
187: 	}
188: 
189: 	if !opts.UseMMap {
190: 		params = append(params, "--no-mmap")
191: 	}
192: 
193: 	if opts.UseNUMA {
194: 		params = append(params, "--numa")
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	// "--cont-batching", // TODO - doesn't seem to have any noticeable perf change for multiple requests
198: 	numParallel := 1
199: 	if onp := os.Getenv("OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL"); onp != "" {
200: 		numParallel, err = strconv.Atoi(onp)
201: 		if err != nil || numParallel <= 0 {
202: 			err = fmt.Errorf("invalid OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=%s must be greater than zero - %w", onp, err)
203: 			slog.Error("misconfiguration", "error", err)
204: 			return nil, err
205: 		}
206: 	}
207: 	params = append(params, "--parallel", fmt.Sprintf("%d", numParallel))
208: 
209: 	for i := 0; i < len(servers); i++ {
210: 		dir := availableServers[servers[i]]
211: 		if dir == "" {
212: 			// Shouldn't happen
213: 			finalErr = fmt.Errorf("[%d] server %s not listed in available servers %v", i, servers[i], availableServers)
214: 			slog.Error("sever list inconsistent", "error", finalErr)
215: 			continue
216: 		}
217: 
218: 		// Find an availableServers  port, retry on each iterration in case the failure was a port conflict race
219: 		port := 0
220: 		if a, err := net.ResolveTCPAddr("tcp", "localhost:0"); err == nil {
221: 			var l *net.TCPListener
222: 			if l, err = net.ListenTCP("tcp", a); err == nil {
223: 				port = l.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port
224: 				l.Close()
225: 			}
226: 		}
227: 		if port == 0 {
228: 			slog.Debug("ResolveTCPAddr failed ", "error", err)
229: 			port = rand.Intn(65535-49152) + 49152 // get a random port in the ephemeral range
230: 		}
231: 		finalParams := append(params, "--port", strconv.Itoa(port))
232: 
233: 		pathEnv := "LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
234: 		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
235: 			pathEnv = "PATH"
236: 		}
237: 		// append the server directory to LD_LIBRARY_PATH/PATH
238: 		libraryPaths := []string{dir}
239: 
240: 		if libraryPath, ok := os.LookupEnv(pathEnv); ok {
241: 			// Append our runner directory to the path
242: 			// This will favor system libraries over our bundled library dependencies
243: 			libraryPaths = append(filepath.SplitList(libraryPath), libraryPaths...)
244: 		}
245: 
246: 		// Note: we always put the dependency path first
247: 		// since this was the exact version we verified for AMD GPUs
248: 		// and we favor what the user had in their path
249: 		if gpus[0].DependencyPath != "" {
250: 			// TODO refine for multi-gpu support
251: 			libraryPaths = append([]string{gpus[0].DependencyPath}, libraryPaths...)
252: 		}
253: 
254: 		server := filepath.Join(dir, "ollama_llama_server")
255: 		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
256: 			server = server + ".exe"
257: 		}
258: 
259: 		// Detect tmp cleaners wiping out the file
260: 		_, err := os.Stat(server)
261: 		if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
262: 			slog.Warn("llama server disappeared, reinitializing payloads", "path", server, "error", err)
263: 			err = Init()
264: 			if err != nil {
265: 				slog.Warn("failed to reinitialize payloads", "error", err)
266: 				return nil, err
267: 			}
268: 		}
269: 
270: 		s := &llmServer{
271: 			port:          port,
272: 			cmd:           exec.Command(server, finalParams...),
273: 			status:        NewStatusWriter(os.Stderr),
274: 			options:       opts,
275: 			estimatedVRAM: estimatedVRAM,
276: 			sem:           semaphore.NewWeighted(int64(numParallel)),
277: 		}
278: 
279: 		libEnv := fmt.Sprintf("%s=%s", pathEnv, strings.Join(libraryPaths, string(filepath.ListSeparator)))
280: 		s.cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), libEnv)
281: 		s.cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
282: 		s.cmd.Stderr = s.status
283: 
284: 		// TODO - multiple GPU selection logic...
285: 		key, val := gpu.GpuInfoList(gpus).GetVisibleDevicesEnv()
286: 		if key != "" {
287: 			s.cmd.Env = append(s.cmd.Env, key+"="+val)
288: 		}
289: 
290: 		slog.Info("starting llama server", "cmd", s.cmd.String())
291: 		// Log at debug as the environment is inherited and might contain sensitive information
292: 		slog.Debug("subprocess", "environment", s.cmd.Env)
293: 
294: 		if err = s.cmd.Start(); err != nil {
295: 			msg := ""
296: 			if s.status != nil && s.status.LastErrMsg != "" {
297: 				msg = s.status.LastErrMsg
298: 			}
299: 			err = fmt.Errorf("error starting the external llama server: %v %s", err, msg)
300: 			finalErr = err
301: 			continue
302: 		}
303: 
304: 		// reap subprocess when it exits
305: 		go func() {
306: 			// Exit status managed via getServerStatus
307: 			_ = s.cmd.Wait()
308: 		}()
309: 
310: 		// TODO - make sure this is all wired up correctly
311: 		// if err = s.WaitUntilRunning(); err != nil {
312: 		// 	slog.Error("error starting llama server", "server", servers[i], "error", err)
313: 		// 	s.Close()
314: 		// 	finalErr = err
315: 		// 	continue
316: 		// }
317: 		return s, nil
318: 	}
319: 
320: 	slog.Error("unable to load any llama server", "error", finalErr)
321: 	return nil, finalErr
322: }

376: func (s *llmServer) getServerStatus(ctx context.Context) (ServerStatus, error) {
377: 	// Fail fast if its exited
378: 	if s.cmd.ProcessState != nil {
379: 		msg := ""
380: 		if s.status != nil && s.status.LastErrMsg != "" {
381: 			msg = s.status.LastErrMsg
382: 		}
383: 		return ServerStatusError, fmt.Errorf("llama runner process no longer running: %d %s", s.cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode(), msg)
384: 	}
385: 
386: 	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/health", s.port), nil)
387: 	if err != nil {
388: 		return ServerStatusError, fmt.Errorf("error creating GET request: %v", err)
389: 	}
390: 	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
391: 
392: 	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
393: 	if err != nil {
394: 		if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
395: 			return ServerStatusNotResponding, fmt.Errorf("server not responding")
396: 		}
397: 		return ServerStatusError, fmt.Errorf("health resp: %w", err)
398: 	}
399: 	defer resp.Body.Close()
400: 
401: 	body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
402: 	if err != nil {
403: 		return ServerStatusError, fmt.Errorf("read health request: %w", err)
404: 	}
405: 
406: 	var status ServerStatusResp
407: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &status); err != nil {
408: 		return ServerStatusError, fmt.Errorf("health unmarshal encode response: %w", err)
409: 	}
410: 
411: 	switch status.Status {
412: 	case "ok":
413: 		return ServerStatusReady, nil
414: 	case "no slot available":
415: 		return ServerStatusNoSlotsAvaialble, nil
416: 	case "loading model":
417: 		return ServerStatusLoadingModel, nil
418: 	default:
419: 		return ServerStatusError, fmt.Errorf("server error: %+v", status)
420: 	}
421: }

432: func (s *llmServer) WaitUntilRunning(ctx context.Context) error {
433: 	start := time.Now()
434: 	// TODO we need to wire up a better way to detect hangs during model load and startup of the server
435: 	expiresAt := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Minute) // be generous with timeout, large models can take a while to load
436: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(50 * time.Millisecond)
437: 	defer ticker.Stop()
438: 
439: 	slog.Info("waiting for llama runner to start responding")
440: 	var lastStatus ServerStatus = -1
441: 	for {
442: 		select {
443: 		case <-ctx.Done():
444: 			slog.Info("context expired before server started")
445: 			return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for llama runner to start: %w", ctx.Err())
446: 		case err := <-s.done:
447: 			msg := ""
448: 			if s.status != nil && s.status.LastErrMsg != "" {
449: 				msg = s.status.LastErrMsg
450: 			}
451: 			return fmt.Errorf("llama runner process has terminated: %v %s", err, msg)
452: 		case <-ticker.C:
453: 			if time.Now().After(expiresAt) {
454: 				// timeout
455: 				msg := ""
456: 				if s.status != nil && s.status.LastErrMsg != "" {
457: 					msg = s.status.LastErrMsg
458: 				}
459: 				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for llama runner to start: %s", msg)
460: 			}
461: 			if s.cmd.ProcessState != nil {
462: 				msg := ""
463: 				if s.status != nil && s.status.LastErrMsg != "" {
464: 					msg = s.status.LastErrMsg
465: 				}
466: 				return fmt.Errorf("llama runner process no longer running: %d %s", s.cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode(), msg)
467: 			}
468: 
469: 			c, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 200*time.Millisecond)
470: 			defer cancel()
471: 			status, err := s.getServerStatus(c)
472: 			if err != nil && lastStatus != status {
473: 				slog.Debug("server not yet available", "error", err)
474: 				lastStatus = status
475: 				continue
476: 			}
477: 
478: 			switch status {
479: 			case ServerStatusLoadingModel:
480: 				// TODO - this state never seems to happen with the current server.cpp code (bug?)
481: 				// it doesn't respond to the health endpoint until after the model is loaded
482: 				slog.Debug("loading model")
483: 			case ServerStatusReady:
484: 				slog.Debug(fmt.Sprintf("llama runner started in %f seconds", time.Since(start).Seconds()))
485: 				return nil
486: 			}
487: 		}
488: 	}
489: }

491: const jsonGrammar = `
492: root   ::= object
493: value  ::= object | array | string | number | ("true" | "false" | "null") ws
494: 
495: object ::=
496:   "{" ws (
497:             string ":" ws value
498:     ("," ws string ":" ws value)*
499:   )? "}" ws
500: 
501: array  ::=
502:   "[" ws (
503:             value
504:     ("," ws value)*
505:   )? "]" ws
506: 
507: string ::=
508:   "\"" (
509:     [^"\\] |
510:     "\\" (["\\/bfnrt] | "u" [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F]) # escapes
511:   )* "\"" ws
512: 
513: number ::= ("-"? ([0-9] | [1-9] [0-9]*)) ("." [0-9]+)? ([eE] [-+]? [0-9]+)? ws
514: 
515: # Optional space: by convention, applied in this grammar after literal chars when allowed
516: ws ::= ([ \t\n] ws)?
517: `

557: func (s *llmServer) Completion(ctx context.Context, req CompletionRequest, fn func(CompletionResponse)) error {
558: 	if err := s.sem.Acquire(ctx, 1); err != nil {
559: 		slog.Error("Failed to acquire semaphore", "error", err)
560: 		return err
561: 	}
562: 	defer s.sem.Release(1)
563: 
564: 	// only allow maximum 10 "context shifts" to avoid infinite generation
565: 	if req.Options.NumPredict < 0 || req.Options.NumPredict > 10*s.options.NumCtx {
566: 		req.Options.NumPredict = 10 * s.options.NumCtx
567: 		slog.Debug("setting token limit to 10x num_ctx", "num_ctx", s.options.NumCtx, "num_predict", req.Options.NumPredict)
568: 	}
569: 
570: 	request := map[string]any{
571: 		"prompt":            req.Prompt,
572: 		"stream":            true,
573: 		"n_predict":         req.Options.NumPredict,
574: 		"n_keep":            req.Options.NumKeep,
575: 		"main_gpu":          req.Options.MainGPU,
576: 		"temperature":       req.Options.Temperature,
577: 		"top_k":             req.Options.TopK,
578: 		"top_p":             req.Options.TopP,
579: 		"tfs_z":             req.Options.TFSZ,
580: 		"typical_p":         req.Options.TypicalP,
581: 		"repeat_last_n":     req.Options.RepeatLastN,
582: 		"repeat_penalty":    req.Options.RepeatPenalty,
583: 		"presence_penalty":  req.Options.PresencePenalty,
584: 		"frequency_penalty": req.Options.FrequencyPenalty,
585: 		"mirostat":          req.Options.Mirostat,
586: 		"mirostat_tau":      req.Options.MirostatTau,
587: 		"mirostat_eta":      req.Options.MirostatEta,
588: 		"penalize_nl":       req.Options.PenalizeNewline,
589: 		"seed":              req.Options.Seed,
590: 		"stop":              req.Options.Stop,
591: 		"image_data":        req.Images,
592: 		"cache_prompt":      true,
593: 	}
594: 
595: 	// Make sure the server is ready
596: 	status, err := s.getServerStatus(ctx)
597: 	if err != nil {
598: 		return err
599: 	} else if status != ServerStatusReady {
600: 		return fmt.Errorf("unexpected server status: %s", status.ToString())
601: 	}
602: 
603: 	if req.Format == "json" {
604: 		request["grammar"] = jsonGrammar
605: 		if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(req.Prompt), "json") {
606: 			slog.Warn("Prompt does not specify that the LLM should response in JSON, but JSON format is expected. For best results specify that JSON is expected in the system prompt.")
607: 		}
608: 	}
609: 
610: 	retryDelay := 100 * time.Microsecond
611: 	for retries := 0; retries < maxRetries; retries++ {
612: 		if retries > 0 {
613: 			time.Sleep(retryDelay) // wait before retrying
614: 			retryDelay *= 2        // exponential backoff
615: 		}
616: 
617: 		// Handling JSON marshaling with special characters unescaped.
618: 		buffer := &bytes.Buffer{}
619: 		enc := json.NewEncoder(buffer)
620: 		enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
621: 
622: 		if err := enc.Encode(request); err != nil {
623: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal data: %v", err)
624: 		}
625: 
626: 		endpoint := fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/completion", s.port)
627: 		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, endpoint, buffer)
628: 		if err != nil {
629: 			return fmt.Errorf("error creating POST request: %v", err)
630: 		}
631: 		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
632: 
633: 		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
634: 		if err != nil {
635: 			return fmt.Errorf("POST predict: %v", err)
636: 		}
637: 		defer resp.Body.Close()
638: 
639: 		if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
640: 			bodyBytes, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
641: 			if err != nil {
642: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed reading llm error response: %w", err)
643: 			}
644: 			log.Printf("llm predict error: %s", bodyBytes)
645: 			return fmt.Errorf("%s", bodyBytes)
646: 		}
647: 
648: 		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
649: 		buf := make([]byte, 0, maxBufferSize)
650: 		scanner.Buffer(buf, maxBufferSize)
651: 
652: 		retryNeeded := false
653: 		// keep track of the last token generated, this is used to abort if the model starts looping
654: 		var lastToken string
655: 		var tokenRepeat int
656: 
657: 		for scanner.Scan() {
658: 			select {
659: 			case <-ctx.Done():
660: 				// This handles the request cancellation
661: 				return ctx.Err()
662: 			default:
663: 				line := scanner.Bytes()
664: 				if len(line) == 0 {
665: 					continue
666: 				}
667: 
668: 				// try again on slot unavailable
669: 				if bytes.Contains(line, []byte("slot unavailable")) {
670: 					retryNeeded = true
671: 					break
672: 				}
673: 
674: 				evt, ok := bytes.CutPrefix(line, []byte("data: "))
675: 				if !ok {
676: 					return fmt.Errorf("error parsing llm response stream: %s", line)
677: 				}
678: 
679: 				var c completion
680: 				if err := json.Unmarshal(evt, &c); err != nil {
681: 					return fmt.Errorf("error unmarshaling llm prediction response: %v", err)
682: 				}
683: 
684: 				switch {
685: 				case strings.TrimSpace(c.Content) == lastToken:
686: 					tokenRepeat++
687: 				default:
688: 					lastToken = strings.TrimSpace(c.Content)
689: 					tokenRepeat = 0
690: 				}
691: 
692: 				// 30 picked as an arbitrary max token repeat limit, modify as needed
693: 				if tokenRepeat > 30 {
694: 					slog.Debug("prediction aborted, token repeat limit reached")
695: 					return ctx.Err()
696: 				}
697: 
698: 				if c.Content != "" {
699: 					fn(CompletionResponse{
700: 						Content: c.Content,
701: 					})
702: 				}
703: 
704: 				if c.Stop {
705: 					fn(CompletionResponse{
706: 						Done:               true,
707: 						PromptEvalCount:    c.Timings.PromptN,
708: 						PromptEvalDuration: parseDurationMs(c.Timings.PromptMS),
709: 						EvalCount:          c.Timings.PredictedN,
710: 						EvalDuration:       parseDurationMs(c.Timings.PredictedMS),
711: 					})
712: 					return nil
713: 				}
714: 			}
715: 		}
716: 
717: 		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
718: 			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unexpected EOF") {
719: 				s.Close()
720: 				msg := ""
721: 				if s.status != nil && s.status.LastErrMsg != "" {
722: 					msg = s.status.LastErrMsg
723: 				}
724: 
725: 				return fmt.Errorf("an unknown error was encountered while running the model %s", msg)
726: 			}
727: 			return fmt.Errorf("error reading llm response: %v", err)
728: 		}
729: 
730: 		if !retryNeeded {
731: 			return nil // success
732: 		}
733: 	}
734: 
735: 	// should never reach here ideally
736: 	return fmt.Errorf("max retries exceeded")
737: }

29: // MissingPart is used to indicate any part of a name that was "promised" by

32: // The value was chosen because it is deemed unlikely to be set by a user,
33: // not a valid part name valid when checked by [Name.IsValid], and easy to

37: // DefaultName returns a name with the default values for the host, namespace,
38: // and tag parts. The model and digest parts are empty.
39: //
40: //   - The default host is ("registry.ollama.ai")
41: //   - The default namespace is ("library")

55: 	kindNamespace
56: 	kindModel
57: 	kindTag

61: func (k partKind) String() string {

63: 	case kindHost:
64: 		return "host"
65: 	case kindNamespace:
66: 		return "namespace"
67: 	case kindModel:

69: 	case kindTag:

78: // Name is a structured representation of a model name string, as defined by
79: // [ParseNameNoDefaults].
80: //
81: // It is not guaranteed to be valid. Use [Name.IsValid] to check if the name
82: // is valid.
83: //
84: // It is not directly comparable with other Names. Use [Name.Equal] and
85: // [Name.MapHash] for determining equality and using as a map key.
86: type Name struct {
87: 	Host      string
88: 	Namespace string
89: 	Model     string
90: 	Tag       string
91: 	RawDigest string
92: }
93: 
94: // ParseName parses and assembles a Name from a name string. The
95: // format of a valid name string is:
96: //
97: //	  s:
98: //		  { host } "/" { namespace } "/" { model } ":" { tag } "@" { digest }
99: //		  { host } "/" { namespace } "/" { model } ":" { tag }
100: //		  { host } "/" { namespace } "/" { model } "@" { digest }
101: //		  { host } "/" { namespace } "/" { model }
102: //		  { namespace } "/" { model } ":" { tag } "@" { digest }
103: //		  { namespace } "/" { model } ":" { tag }
104: //		  { namespace } "/" { model } "@" { digest }
105: //		  { namespace } "/" { model }
106: //		  { model } ":" { tag } "@" { digest }
107: //		  { model } ":" { tag }
108: //		  { model } "@" { digest }
109: //		  { model }
110: //		  "@" { digest }
111: //	  host:
112: //	      pattern: alphanum-or-underscore { alphanum | "-" | "_" | "." | ":" }*
113: //	      length:  [1, 350]
114: //	  namespace:
115: //	      pattern: alphanum-or-underscore { alphanum | "-" | "_" }*
116: //	      length:  [1, 80]
117: //	  model:
118: //	      pattern: alphanum-or-underscore { alphanum | "-" | "_" | "." }*
119: //	      length:  [1, 80]
120: //	  tag:
121: //	      pattern: alphanum-or-underscore { alphanum | "-" | "_" | "." }*
122: //	      length:  [1, 80]
123: //	  digest:
124: //	      pattern: alphanum-or-underscore { alphanum | "-" | ":" }*
125: //	      length:  [1, 80]
126: //
127: // Most users should use [ParseName] instead, unless need to support
128: // different defaults than DefaultName.
129: //
130: // The name returned is not guaranteed to be valid. If it is not valid, the
131: // field values are left in an undefined state. Use [Name.IsValid] to check
132: // if the name is valid.
133: func ParseName(s string) Name {
134: 	return Merge(ParseNameBare(s), DefaultName())
135: }

137: // ParseNameBare parses s as a name string and returns a Name. No merge with
138: // [DefaultName] is performed.
139: func ParseNameBare(s string) Name {
140: 	var n Name
141: 	var promised bool
142: 
143: 	s, n.RawDigest, promised = cutLast(s, "@")
144: 	if promised && n.RawDigest == "" {
145: 		n.RawDigest = MissingPart
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	s, n.Tag, _ = cutPromised(s, ":")
149: 	s, n.Model, promised = cutPromised(s, "/")
150: 	if !promised {
151: 		n.Model = s
152: 		return n
153: 	}
154: 	s, n.Namespace, promised = cutPromised(s, "/")
155: 	if !promised {
156: 		n.Namespace = s
157: 		return n
158: 	}
159: 	n.Host = s
160: 
161: 	return n
162: }

164: // Merge merges the host, namespace, and tag parts of the two names,
165: // preferring the non-empty parts of a.
166: func Merge(a, b Name) Name {
167: 	a.Host = cmp.Or(a.Host, b.Host)
168: 	a.Namespace = cmp.Or(a.Namespace, b.Namespace)
169: 	a.Tag = cmp.Or(a.Tag, b.Tag)
170: 	return a
171: }

173: // String returns the name string, in the format that [ParseNameNoDefaults]
174: // accepts as valid, if [Name.IsValid] reports true; otherwise the empty
175: // string is returned.
176: func (n Name) String() string {
177: 	var b strings.Builder
178: 	if n.Host != "" {
179: 		b.WriteString(n.Host)
180: 		b.WriteByte('/')
181: 	}
182: 	if n.Namespace != "" {
183: 		b.WriteString(n.Namespace)
184: 		b.WriteByte('/')
185: 	}
186: 	b.WriteString(n.Model)
187: 	if n.Tag != "" {

189: 		b.WriteString(n.Tag)
190: 	}
191: 	if n.RawDigest != "" {
192: 		b.WriteByte('@')

195: 	return b.String()
196: }

198: // IsValid reports whether all parts of the name are present and valid. The

201: 	if n.RawDigest != "" && !isValidPart(kindDigest, n.RawDigest) {

210: 	var parts = []string{
211: 		n.Host,
212: 		n.Namespace,
213: 		n.Model,
214: 		n.Tag,
215: 	}
216: 	for i, part := range parts {
217: 		if !isValidPart(partKind(i), part) {

219: 		}
220: 	}
221: 	return true

224: // Filepath returns a canonical filepath that represents the name with each part from
225: // host to tag as a directory in the form:
226: //
227: //	{host}/{namespace}/{model}/{tag}
228: //
229: // It uses the system's filepath separator and ensures the path is clean.
230: //
231: // It panics if the name is not fully qualified. Use [Name.IsFullyQualified]
232: // to check if the name is fully qualified.

235: 		panic("illegal attempt to get filepath of invalid name")
236: 	}
237: 	return filepath.Join(
238: 		strings.ToLower(filepath.Join(

252: func isValidLen(kind partKind, s string) bool {
253: 	switch kind {
254: 	case kindHost:
255: 		return len(s) >= 1 && len(s) <= 350
256: 	case kindTag:
257: 		return len(s) >= 1 && len(s) <= 80
258: 	default:
259: 		return len(s) >= 1 && len(s) <= 80
260: 	}
261: }
262: 
263: func isValidPart(kind partKind, s string) bool {
264: 	if !isValidLen(kind, s) {
265: 		return false
266: 	}
267: 	for i := range s {
268: 		if i == 0 {
269: 			if !isAlphanumericOrUnderscore(s[i]) {
270: 				return false
271: 			}
272: 			continue
273: 		}
274: 		switch s[i] {
275: 		case '_', '-':
276: 		case '.':
277: 			if kind == kindNamespace {
278: 				return false
279: 			}
280: 		case ':':
281: 			if kind != kindHost && kind != kindDigest {
282: 				return false
283: 			}
284: 		default:
285: 			if !isAlphanumeric(s[i]) {
286: 				return false
287: 			}
288: 		}
289: 	}
290: 	return true
291: }
292: 
293: func isAlphanumeric(c byte) bool {
294: 	return c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' || c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' || c >= '0' && c <= '9'
295: }
296: 
297: func isAlphanumericOrUnderscore(c byte) bool {
298: 	return c == '_' || isAlphanumeric(c)
299: }
300: 
301: func cutLast(s, sep string) (before, after string, ok bool) {
302: 	i := strings.LastIndex(s, sep)
303: 	if i >= 0 {
304: 		return s[:i], s[i+len(sep):], true
305: 	}
306: 	return s, "", false
307: }
308: 
309: // cutPromised cuts the last part of s at the last occurrence of sep. If sep is
310: // found, the part before and after sep are returned as-is unless empty, in
311: // which case they are returned as MissingPart, which will cause
312: // [Name.IsValid] to return false.
313: func cutPromised(s, sep string) (before, after string, ok bool) {
314: 	before, after, ok = cutLast(s, sep)
315: 	if !ok {
316: 		return before, after, false
317: 	}
318: 	return cmp.Or(before, MissingPart), cmp.Or(after, MissingPart), true
319: }

361: 	type predKey struct {
362: 		Library string
363: 		ID      string
364: 	}
365: 	predMap := map[predKey]uint64{} // Sum up the total predicted usage per GPU for all runners
366: 	s.loadedMu.Lock()
367: 	for _, r := range s.loaded {
368: 		r.refMu.Lock()
369: 		gpuIDs := make([]string, 0, len(r.gpus))
370: 		if r.llama != nil {
371: 
372: 			// TODO this should be broken down by GPU instead of assuming uniform spread
373: 			estimatedVRAMPerGPU := r.llama.EstimatedVRAM() / uint64(len(r.gpus))
374: 			for _, gpu := range r.gpus {
375: 				gpuIDs = append(gpuIDs, gpu.ID)
376: 			}
377: 			for _, gpu := range allGpus {
378: 				if slices.Contains(gpuIDs, gpu.ID) {
379: 					predMap[predKey{gpu.Library, gpu.ID}] += estimatedVRAMPerGPU
380: 				}
381: 			}
382: 		} else {
383: 			slog.Warn("unexpected nil runner reference, memory prediction may be incorrect")
384: 		}
385: 		r.refMu.Unlock()
386: 	}
387: 	s.loadedMu.Unlock()
388: 
389: 	// Now that we've summed up all the GPU usage predictions across all the loaded runners, update the gpu list
390: 	for i := range allGpus {
391: 		if p, ok := predMap[predKey{allGpus[i].Library, allGpus[i].ID}]; ok {
392: 			slog.Debug("gpu reported", "gpu", allGpus[i].ID, "library", allGpus[i].Library, "available", format.HumanBytes2(allGpus[i].FreeMemory))
393: 			if p > allGpus[i].TotalMemory {
394: 				// Shouldn't happen
395: 				slog.Warn("predicted usage exceeds VRAM", "gpu", allGpus[i].ID, "totalMemory", allGpus[i].TotalMemory, "predicted", p)
396: 				allGpus[i].FreeMemory = 0
397: 			} else if (allGpus[i].TotalMemory - p) < allGpus[i].FreeMemory { // predicted free is smaller than reported free, use it
398: 				// TODO maybe we should just always trust our numbers, since cuda's free memory reporting is laggy
399: 				// and we might unload models we didn't actually need to.  The risk is if some other GPU intensive app is loaded
400: 				// after we start our first runner, then we'll never acount for that, so picking the smallest free value seems prudent.
401: 				allGpus[i].FreeMemory = allGpus[i].TotalMemory - p
402: 			}

1: # Ollama Windows Preview
2: 
3: Welcome to the Ollama Windows preview.
4: 
5: No more WSL required!
6: 
7: Ollama now runs as a native Windows application, including NVIDIA and AMD Radeon GPU support.
8: After installing Ollama Windows Preview, Ollama will run in the background and
9: the `ollama` command line is available in `cmd`, `powershell` or your favorite
10: terminal application. As usual the Ollama [api](./api.md) will be served on
11: `http://localhost:11434`.
12: 
13: As this is a preview release, you should expect a few bugs here and there.  If
14: you run into a problem you can reach out on
15: [Discord](https://discord.gg/ollama), or file an 
16: [issue](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues).
17: Logs will often be helpful in diagnosing the problem (see
18: [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) below)
19: 
20: ## System Requirements
21: 
22: * Windows 10 or newer, Home or Pro
23: * NVIDIA 452.39 or newer Drivers if you have an NVIDIA card
24: * AMD Radeon Driver https://www.amd.com/en/support if you have a Radeon card
25: 
26: ## API Access
27: 
28: Here's a quick example showing API access from `powershell`
29: ```powershell
30: (Invoke-WebRequest -method POST -Body '{"model":"llama2", "prompt":"Why is the sky blue?", "stream": false}' -uri http://localhost:11434/api/generate ).Content | ConvertFrom-json
31: ```
32: 
33: ## Troubleshooting
34: 
35: While we're in preview, `OLLAMA_DEBUG` is always enabled, which adds
36: a "view logs" menu item to the app, and increses logging for the GUI app and
37: server.
38: 
39: Ollama on Windows stores files in a few different locations.  You can view them in
40: the explorer window by hitting `<cmd>+R` and type in:
41: - `explorer %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama` contains logs, and downloaded updates
42:     - *app.log* contains logs from the GUI application
43:     - *server.log* contains the server logs
44:     - *upgrade.log* contains log output for upgrades
45: - `explorer %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Ollama` contains the binaries (The installer adds this to your user PATH)
46: - `explorer %HOMEPATH%\.ollama` contains models and configuration
47: - `explorer %TEMP%` contains temporary executable files in one or more `ollama*` directories
48: ## Standalone CLI
49: 
50: The easiest way to install Ollama on Windows is via the `OllamaSetup.exe`
51: installer.  The installer sets up Ollama for the current user without needing
52: Administrator rights and also provides automatic updates.
53: 
54: If you would prefer to install Ollama to facilitate integration into existing
55: applications, or if you wish to run it as a system service, a standalone zip
56: archive is also available: `ollama-windows-amd64.zip`.  This archive contains
57: only the Ollama CLI and GPU library dependencies for Nvidia and AMD, which makes
58: it easy to embed Ollama in existing applications or run it as a system service
59: via `ollama serve` with tools like [NSSM](https://nssm.cc/).

+// Free memory reporting on GPUs can lag for a while even after the runner
+// exits, so we have to keep checking until we see the available memory recover,
+// otherwise subsequent model loads will get far less layers loaded or worse
+// case, may completely fall back to CPU mode.
+// This routine must be called before the runner unloads so it can establish
+// a before and after GPU memory allocation.  The returned channel
+// will be notified when we're done waiting, or have timed out and should
+// proceed anyway
+func (runner *runnerRef) waitForVRAMRecovery() chan interface{} {
+	finished := make(chan interface{}, 1)
+
+	// CPU or Metal don't need checking, so no waiting required
+	if len(runner.gpus) == 1 && (runner.gpus[0].Library == "cpu" || runner.gpus[0].Library == "metal") {
+		finished <- struct{}{}
+		return finished
+	}
+	start := time.Now()
+
+	// Establish a baseline before we unload
+	gpusBefore := gpu.GetGPUInfo()
+	var totalMemoryBefore, freeMemoryBefore uint64
+	for _, gpu := range gpusBefore {
+		totalMemoryBefore += gpu.TotalMemory
+		freeMemoryBefore += gpu.FreeMemory
+	}
+	go func() {
+		expiresAt := start.Add(5 * time.Second) // typical convergence is 0.5-1.5s
+		ticker := time.NewTicker(250 * time.Millisecond)
+		defer ticker.Stop()
+		for {
+			<-ticker.C
+			if time.Now().After(expiresAt) {
+				slog.Warn("gpu VRAM usage didn't recover within timeout", "seconds", time.Since(start).Seconds())
+				finished <- struct{}{}
+			}
+
+			// Query GPUs, look for free to go back up
+			gpusNow := gpu.GetGPUInfo()
+			var totalMemoryNow, freeMemoryNow uint64
+			for _, gpu := range gpusNow {
+				totalMemoryNow += gpu.TotalMemory
+				freeMemoryNow += gpu.FreeMemory
+			}
+			// If we're within ~80% of the estimated memory usage recovered, bail out
+			if float32(freeMemoryNow-freeMemoryBefore) > float32(runner.estimatedVRAM)*0.8 {
+				slog.Debug(fmt.Sprintf("gpu VRAM free memory converged after %0.2f seconds", time.Since(start).Seconds()))
+				finished <- struct{}{}
+				return
+			}
+		}
+	}()
+	return finished
+
+}
